mainTopic: Marriage timing and good deeds, the 'him and them' מחלוקת, and the new משנה on murderers killed by the sword
overview: The amud opens by explaining that רב כהנא's 'wicked, crafty poor man' is a father who delays marrying off his grown daughter. It also brings רבי עקיבא's warning to beware of advice that serves the adviser. רב teaches that marrying a daughter to an old man, marrying a wife to a young son, or returning a lost item to a נכרי is condemned by a harsh פסוק. A ברייתא praising marriage close to maturity is shown not to contradict him. Another ברייתא lists kind acts whose reward is that ה׳ answers prayers. Then רבי ישמעאל and רבי עקיבא argue over the words ״אֹתוֹ וְאֶתְהֶן״, and אביי and רבא each explain what the difference between them is. A new משנה begins on those killed by the sword: the רוצח and the people of an עיר הנדחת. It separates direct killing, which is חייב, from indirect causing, which is פטור. The גמרא explains why iron has no size requirement, why holding someone down counts as killing, and starts רבינא's קל וחומר about confining an animal in the sun. That קל וחומר continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Who is the poor man who is wicked and crafty
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains רב כהנא's statement: the 'wicked, crafty poor man' is a father who delays marrying off his grown daughter.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what he means: Who is a poor man who is wicked and crafty? One who delays marrying off his grown daughter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא clears up a difficulty raised just before this line by explaining what רב כהנא really meant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'wicked, crafty poor man' is defined through one specific case: a father who holds back his בוגרת daughter from marriage. This connects to the earlier discussion about delaying a daughter's marriage, which can lead her to sin.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what he means: the גמרא is re-reading a statement
A poor man who is wicked and crafty
A girl who has passed into full adulthood

phrases.english: This is what he is saying:
Who is a poor man who is wicked and crafty?
This is one who delays the marriage of his daughter who is a grown woman.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves a difficulty from the previous discussion of רב כהנא's statement.
steps.terutzMaskana: The 'wicked, crafty poor man' means a father who delays his grown daughter's marriage.

steps.title: Beware of advice that serves the adviser
steps.stepSummary: Another teaching of רב כהנא in the name of רבי עקיבא: be careful of someone whose advice fits his own interests.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא said in the name of רבי עקיבא: Be careful of someone who advises you according to his own interests.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another, separate teaching from the same speakers, רב כהנא in the name of רבי עקיבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is new wisdom, not a continuation of the argument. It warns that advice can be shaped by what helps the adviser.

keyTerms.meaning: According to his own way, meaning his own interests

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַב כָּהֲנָא מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא:
phrases.english: And Rav Kahana said in the name of Rabbi Akiva:
Be careful of one who advises you
according to his own way.
phrases.notes: He means advice that fits what is good for the adviser himself.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב כָּהֲנָא מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new teaching added because it has the same speakers as the previous one.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Be careful of advice given for the adviser's own benefit.

steps.title: Three people who cause sin
steps.stepSummary: רב teaches that marrying a daughter to an old man, marrying a wife to a young son, and returning a lost item to a נכרי are described by a harsh פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: One who marries his daughter to an old man, one who marries a wife to his young son, and one who returns a lost item to a נכרי, about him the פסוק says: 'To add the watered to the thirsty; ה׳ will not be willing to forgive him.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a teaching of רב listing three behaviors and applying a harsh פסוק to each.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each case causes a problem. In the two marriage cases the wife is left unsatisfied, which can lead to sin, and returning lost property to a נכרי adds to someone else's wealth when there is no obligation to do so. The פסוק from דברים describes someone the תורה says ה׳ will not forgive.

keyTerms.meaning: A minor, someone not yet grown up

steps.confusionAlert: Only the case of the young son will be challenged in the next step. The other two cases are not questioned here.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
One who marries his daughter to an old man,
and one who marries a wife to his minor son,
and one who returns a lost item to a gentile –
about him the verse says:
"To add the watered to the thirsty.
The Lord will not be willing to forgive him."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new teaching connected to the topic of bad marriage timing for children.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Marrying a daughter to an old man, marrying a wife to a young son, and returning a lost item to a נכרי are condemned by the פסוק.

steps.title: A ברייתא praises marrying children young
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא praises someone who marries off his children close to maturity, which seems to contradict רב's criticism of marrying off a young son.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged from a ברייתא: One who loves his wife like himself, honors her more than himself, guides his sons and daughters on a straight path, and marries them off close to maturity, about him the פסוק says: 'And you will know that your tent is at peace; you will visit your home and not sin.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב's teaching using a ברייתא that praises marrying children off young.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב said that marrying a wife to a young son leads to sin. This ברייתא says that marrying children off young brings peace to the home. So young marriage looks like a good thing, not a bad thing.

keyTerms.meaning: They challenged, from a תנאי source
Close to their age of maturity

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
One who loves his wife like himself,
and who honors her more than himself,
and who guides his sons and daughters on a straight path,
and who marries them off close to their maturity –
about him the verse says:
"And you will know that your tent is at peace;
and you will visit your home and not sin."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the 'young son' part of רב's teaching.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's statement that marrying a wife to one's young son causes sin.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא praises marrying children off young, so young marriage seems to be a good thing.

steps.title: Close to maturity is different
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers: marrying children off close to maturity is not the same as marrying off a young child.
steps.simpleTranslation: Close to their maturity is different.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by showing that the two cases are different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב criticized marrying off a son who is still a קטן. The ברייתא praises marrying off children who are just about to reach maturity, so there is only a short wait and little risk of sin. Both teachings stand.
steps.whatToRemember: Marrying a son off while he is a קטן is criticized, but marrying children off close to their maturity is praised.

phrases.english: Close to their maturity – is different.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the ברייתא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to praise young marriage in general, against רב.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא praises marriage close to maturity. רב criticizes marriage while the son is still young, so there is no contradiction.

steps.title: People whose prayers are answered
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא lists kind behaviors: loving neighbors, bringing relatives close, marrying one's sister's daughter, and lending to a poor man in need. About these people the פסוק says ה׳ will answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: One who loves his neighbors, brings his relatives close, marries his sister's daughter, and lends a סלע to a poor man in his time of need, about him the פסוק says: 'Then you will call and ה׳ will answer.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with a positive list, the opposite of רב's negative list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each behavior shows closeness and care for people near you, and helping the poor exactly when they need it most. The reward, from ישעיהו, is that ה׳ answers this person's prayers.
steps.whatToRemember: Caring for the people close to you, and helping the poor exactly when they need it, earns the promise that ה׳ will answer your prayers.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
One who loves his neighbors,
and one who brings his relatives close,
and one who marries the daughter of his sister,
and one who lends a sela to a poor man in his time of need –
about him the verse says:
"Then you will call, and the Lord will answer."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new ברייתא with a positive list, set against the earlier negative list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who cares for neighbors and relatives, marries his sister's daughter, and lends to the poor in need will have his prayers answered.

steps.title: How to read the words "him and them"
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא brings a מחלוקת. רבי ישמעאל says ״אֹתוֹ וְאֶתְהֶן״ means "him and one of them." רבי עקיבא says it means "him and both of them."
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: "Him and them" means him and one of them. These are the words of רבי ישמעאל. רבי עקיבא says: him and both of them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא where two תנאים disagree about the words ״אֹתוֹ וְאֶתְהֶן״ in the פסוק about a man who lives with a woman and her mother.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says the man and "them" are burned. רבי ישמעאל says only one of the women is meant, since the other is his own wife. רבי עקיבא says the word covers two women.

keyTerms.meaning: The רבנן taught. This opens a ברייתא.
"Him and them." The words in the פסוק being discussed.
Burning. One of the four death penalties of בית דין, given in this פסוק.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
"Him and them"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 20:14. The פסוק is about a man who takes a woman and her mother.

phrases.english: means him and one of them,
these are the words of Rabbi Yishmael.
Rabbi Akiva says:
Him and both of them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic. It moves from the aggadic teachings of steps 2 to 6 to a halachic דרשה about the death penalty.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי ישמעאל: ״אֹתוֹ וְאֶתְהֶן״ means him and one of them. רבי עקיבא: him and both of them.

steps.title: What is the practical difference between them?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what real difference comes out of the מחלוקת between רבי ישמעאל and רבי עקיבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what these two תנאים actually disagree about in practice. This question sets up the two answers that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even רבי עקיבא would not punish the man's innocent wife. So "both of them" cannot simply mean the wife and the mother-in-law. That makes the two opinions look the same, so the גמרא asks where they really differ.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difference between them? It asks for the practical result of a מחלוקת.

phrases.english: What is the difference between them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the practical difference behind the מחלוקת in step 7.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What practical or interpretive difference separates רבי ישמעאל and רבי עקיבא?

steps.title: אביי: They disagree about how to read the פסוק
steps.stepSummary: אביי says the difference is only in how they read the פסוק. For רבי ישמעאל, the mother-in-law's mother is learned from a דרשה. For רבי עקיבא, she is written right here in this פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: The difference between them is how they read the meaning of the פסוק. רבי ישמעאל holds that "him and them" means him and one of them, because in Greek they call "one" heina. So the mother-in-law's mother is learned from a דרשה. רבי עקיבא holds that "him and them" means him and both of them, so the mother-in-law's mother is written here.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers that the two תנאים agree on the law. They only disagree about where in the תורה the איסור of the mother-in-law's mother comes from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ישמעאל reads ״אֶתְהֶן״ as "one," based on the Greek word ״הִינָא״. So the פסוק only speaks about the mother-in-law, and her mother is learned from a דרשה. רבי עקיבא reads it as "both," meaning the mother-in-law and her mother. So both are written openly in this פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: How they read the meaning of the פסוק.
It comes from a דרשה, not from an open פסוק.

steps.confusionAlert: For אביי, both תנאים agree that the mother-in-law's mother is forbidden with the same punishment. They only argue about where that איסור comes from.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
The difference between them is how they read the meaning of the verse.
Rabbi Yishmael holds:
"Him and them" means him and one of them,
because in the Greek language
they call "one" heina.
phrases.notes: ״הִינָא״ sounds like the ending ״הֶן״ in ״וְאֶתְהֶן״. That is why רבי ישמעאל reads it as "one."

phrases.english: And his mother-in-law's mother is learned from a derivation.
Rabbi Akiva holds:
"Him and them" means him and both of them,
and his mother-in-law's mother is written here.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: מַשְׁמָעוּת דּוֹרְשִׁים אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: There is no difference in the law. The only difference is whether the mother-in-law's mother comes from a דרשה (רבי ישמעאל) or is written in this פסוק (רבי עקיבא).

steps.title: רבא: They disagree about the mother-in-law after the wife dies
steps.stepSummary: רבא gives a different answer. The difference is a man who lives with his mother-in-law after his wife has died. רבי ישמעאל says he gets שריפה. רבי עקיבא says it is only an איסור.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The difference between them is his mother-in-law after death. רבי ישמעאל holds that his mother-in-law after death is punished with burning. רבי עקיבא holds that it is just a prohibition.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a second, different answer to "what is the difference?" For him, the מחלוקת has a real practical result.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי ישמעאל, "him and one of them" means even one of the pair (wife or mother-in-law) is enough. So if his wife has died, he still gets שריפה for his mother-in-law. For רבי עקיבא, after the wife's death there is no death penalty, only a plain איסור.

keyTerms.meaning: After death. Here it means after his wife has died.
Just a prohibition, with no death penalty.

steps.whatToRemember: There are two answers to "what is the difference?" אביי: it is only about how to read the פסוק. רבא: it is a practical difference about the mother-in-law after the wife dies. רבי ישמעאל gives שריפה, and רבי עקיבא calls it only an איסור.
steps.whyThisMatters: רבא's answer turns a disagreement over one word into a real difference about whether בית דין puts someone to death.

phrases.english: Rava said:
The difference between them is his mother-in-law after death.
phrases.notes: He means after his wife has died.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yishmael holds:
his mother-in-law after death is punished by burning,
and Rabbi Akiva holds:
it is just a prohibition.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: חֲמוֹתוֹ לְאַחַר מִיתָה אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different answer from אביי's (step 9) to the question of step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The difference is a man who lives with his mother-in-law after his wife's death. רבי ישמעאל says שריפה. רבי עקיבא says only an איסור.

steps.title: New משנה: Who is killed by the sword
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists the people who get the death penalty of הרג: the רוצח and the people of an עיר הנדחת.
steps.simpleTranslation: And these are the ones killed by the sword: the murderer, and the people of a city that was led into idol worship.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins, moving from people who get שריפה to people who get הרג, the sword. It names two groups.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier the משנה listed the people who get burned. Now it lists a different court death, הרג. Only two groups get it: a murderer, and the people of a city that went after עבודה זרה.

keyTerms.meaning: Those killed by the sword (the death penalty of הֶרֶג)
A city led astray into idol worship

phrases.english: MISHNA: And these are the ones who are killed [by the sword]:
The murderer, and the people of a city led astray [into idol worship].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה. It moves on from the שריפה discussion in Steps 9-10 to the next court death, הרג.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The רוצח and the people of an עיר הנדחת are killed by the sword.

steps.title: When a murderer is liable
steps.stepSummary: Someone who strikes with stone or iron, or holds a person down in water or fire so he cannot get out and dies, is חייב.
steps.simpleTranslation: A murderer who hit his fellow with a stone or with iron, or pressed him down into water or into fire, and the victim could not get out and died, is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה defines the murderer it just mentioned. It gives examples of killing directly, which makes a person חייב the death penalty.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every case here is a direct killing. Either the killer hits with a weapon, or he physically holds the victim where he cannot escape. Because the victim had no way out, the death is fully the killer's doing.

phrases.english: A murderer who struck his fellow
with a stone or with iron,
or held him down in the water
or in the fire,
and he cannot get out from there,
phrases.notes: This is talking about the victim.

phrases.english: and he died, he is liable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains what kind of killing makes someone the רוצח listed in Step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Direct killing, whether by a weapon or by holding the victim in a place he cannot escape, makes one חייב.

steps.title: Cases where the killer is exempt
steps.stepSummary: Pushing someone in when he could have gotten out, or setting a dog or snake on him, makes the person פטור.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he pushed him into water or fire and the victim could have gotten out, but he died, the pusher is exempt. If he set a dog on him, or set a snake on him, he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now gives the opposite side: cases that look like killing but where the person is פטור from the court's death penalty.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the pushing case the victim could have saved himself, so the pusher did not really kill him. In the dog and snake cases an animal did the killing on its own, so the person only caused the death indirectly.

keyTerms.meaning: Set on, sicced (an animal on someone)

steps.confusionAlert: פטור here means the court does not execute him. It does not mean what he did is allowed.

phrases.english: If he pushed him into the water
or into the fire,
and he could have gotten out from there,
and he died, he is exempt.
If he set the dog on him,
or set the snake on him, he is exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּחָפוֹ לְתוֹךְ הַמַּיִם אוֹ לְתוֹךְ הָאוּר, וְיָכוֹל לַעֲלוֹת מִשָּׁם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The opposite of Step 12. These are cases where the death is not counted as a direct killing.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the victim could have escaped, or an animal did the killing, the person is פטור.

steps.title: Making a snake bite: a dispute
steps.stepSummary: If he made the snake bite the victim, רבי יהודה says he is חייב and the חכמים say he is פטור.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he made the snake bite him, רבי יהודה holds him liable, and the Sages exempt him.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה ends with a case in the middle: the person actually pressed the snake's bite into the victim. רבי יהודה and the חכמים argue about it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is closer than just setting the snake on someone, because he physically made the bite happen. רבי יהודה treats it as killing with his own hands. The חכמים still see the snake as the real killer, so it is only causing death indirectly.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא who here holds the person liable

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's line is this: direct killing makes a person חייב, and indirect causing makes him פטור. The snake bite is the case they argue about.

phrases.english: If he made the snake bite him:
Rabbi Yehuda holds him liable,
and the Sages exempt him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes one step past the snake case in Step 13, to a case where the person made the bite himself.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Making a snake bite: רבי יהודה says חייב, the חכמים say פטור.

steps.title: Why the Torah gives no size requirement for iron
steps.stepSummary: שמואל explains that the פסוק says "יד" for stone and wood but not for iron, because iron of any size can kill.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: Why was "hand" not said about iron? Because iron kills in any amount.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins with the iron weapon mentioned in the משנה. שמואל explains a detail in the פסוקים about murder weapons.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For a stone and a wooden tool, the תורה adds the word "יד". This means the object must be big enough to kill. For iron, the תורה leaves that word out. שמואל says this is because even a tiny piece of iron can kill, so no minimum size is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה
"Hand", a word in the פסוק that sets a size requirement
In any amount, no matter how small

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that for an iron weapon, the court does not need to check whether it was big enough to kill.

phrases.english: GEMARA: Shmuel said:
Why was "hand" not stated regarding iron?
phrases.notes: במדבר 35:17-18 says "יד" for a stone and for a wooden tool. במדבר 35:16, about iron, leaves it out.

phrases.english: Because iron kills in any amount.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא on the new משנה. It explains the iron weapon from Step 12 by looking at the פסוקים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Iron has no minimum size for murder, because iron of any size can kill.

steps.title: A ברייתא backs up שמואל: iron kills in any size
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי saying that ה' knows iron of any size can kill, so the Torah gave it no minimum size.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is also taught in a ברייתא: רבי says, It is revealed and known before the One Who spoke and the world came to be that iron kills in any amount. That is why the Torah gave no minimum size for it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that says the same thing שמואל said in the last step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל explained why the פסוק gives no 'יד' size for iron. Now a ברייתא from רבי gives the same idea: iron can kill no matter how small, so there is no measure. This supports שמואל's reading.

keyTerms.meaning: It is also taught this way (a ברייתא that supports what was just said)
In any amount, no matter how small
A required minimum size or amount

phrases.english: It is also taught this way:
Rabbi says,
It is revealed and known before
the One Who spoke and the world came into being
that iron kills in any amount,

phrases.aramaic: לְפִיכָךְ לֹא נָתְנָה תּוֹרָה בּוֹ שִׁיעוּר.
phrases.english: therefore the Torah did not give it a measure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports שמואל's explanation from step 15 with a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: שמואל's claim that iron has no size requirement because any size can kill.

steps.title: This only applies when he stabbed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא limits the rule: iron needs no size only when the killer stabbed with it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this only applies when he stabbed him with it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a limit to the rule that iron of any size makes one liable.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A tiny piece of iron can kill by piercing, but not by hitting. So the 'no size' rule is only for stabbing. If he just struck with iron, it would need to be big enough to kill.

keyTerms.meaning: And these words apply only... (a limiting phrase)
When he stabbed or pierced him

phrases.english: And this applies only
when he stabbed him.
phrases.notes: Literally 'pierced him a piercing,' meaning he stuck the iron in, not just hit with it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the rule just proven in step 16.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Iron of any size makes one liable only when it was used to stab; striking still needs a size that can kill.
steps.whatToRemember: Iron has no minimum size because it can kill in any amount, but only when used to stab.

steps.title: Both halves of the משנה teach something new: the first half
steps.stepSummary: Quoting 'held him down in the water,' the גמרא says each half of the משנה has a new point. The first half: even if he did not push him in, he is liable since the victim could not get out.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Or held him down in the water.' The first part teaches a new point and the last part teaches a new point. The first part teaches: even though he was not the one who pushed him in, since the victim could not get out and died, he is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה about water and starts showing what is new in each half, beginning with the first half.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You might think only someone who pushed the victim in is a killer. The first half teaches that holding him down is enough, even without pushing. What matters is that the victim could not escape.

keyTerms.meaning: The first part of the משנה
The last part of the משנה
It teaches us a new point (a surprising חידוש)

phrases.english: 'Or held him down in the water.'
phrases.notes: The גמרא is quoting the משנה from step 12.

phrases.english: The first part teaches us a new point,
and the last part teaches us a new point.
The first part teaches us a new point:

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דְּלָאו אִיהוּ דְּחָפוֹ,
phrases.english: even though he was not the one who pushed him in,

phrases.aramaic: כֵּיוָן דְּאֵין יָכוֹל לַעֲלוֹת מִשָּׁם וָמֵת –
phrases.english: since he could not get out from there and died,
he is liable.

steps.triggerLanguage: רֵישָׁא רְבוּתָא קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן, וְסֵיפָא רְבוּתָא קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new line of the משנה, the case of holding someone in water.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Holding someone down so he cannot escape makes one liable even if he did not push him in.

steps.title: The new point of the second half
steps.stepSummary: The last half teaches that even if he pushed the victim in, he is פטור if the victim could have gotten out.
steps.simpleTranslation: The last part teaches a new point: even though he pushed him in, since the victim could have gotten out and still died, he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its explanation by showing the new point of the second half of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You might think pushing someone into water is surely murder. The second half teaches that if he could have climbed out, the pusher is פטור. Together, both halves show that the key question is whether the victim could escape, not who pushed.

phrases.english: The last part teaches us a new point:
even though he pushed him in,
since he could have gotten out from there, and he died,
he is exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the two-part explanation begun in step 18.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Pushing someone in is פטור if the victim could have escaped.
steps.whatToRemember: In the water cases, what decides liability is whether the victim could get out, not whether the attacker pushed him.

steps.title: Where do we learn that holding someone down is liable?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source that someone who held a victim down is liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: Holding down: where do we learn it from?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a source in the תורה for the rule that holding someone down makes one liable. This sets up שמואל's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Holding someone down is not a direct blow like hitting with a stone or iron. So the גמרא wants a פסוק showing it still counts as murder.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we learn this?

phrases.english: Holding down: from where do we learn it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the Torah source behind the ruling in step 18.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A פסוק showing that one who holds a victim down so he dies is liable.

steps.title: שמואל: 'או באיבה' includes one who confines
steps.stepSummary: שמואל learns from the words 'או באיבה' that someone who confines a victim is also liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: The פסוק says 'Or in enmity,' to include someone who confines another.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל answers the question by pointing to the words 'או באיבה' in the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל reads the phrase 'או באיבה' as widening the kinds of killing that count. He uses it to include someone who traps or holds a person in a place where he cannot survive, even without striking him.

keyTerms.meaning: One who confines or traps someone

phrases.english: Shmuel said:
For the verse says 'Or in enmity,'
to include one who confines.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 20.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The words 'או באיבה' include one who confines a victim so he dies.

steps.title: Confining someone else's animal in the sun
steps.stepSummary: A man confined another person's animal in the sun and it died. רבינא made him pay; רב אחא בר רב said he is פטור.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a man who confined his friend's animal in the sun, and it died. רבינא held him liable; רב אחא בר רב exempted him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells of a real case about confining, this time an animal and money damages, and brings two opinions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This takes the idea of 'confining' from murder to damages. The sun killed the animal, not the man directly. רבינא says trapping it there is enough to make him pay; רב אחא בר רב says he did not do the killing, so he is פטור.

phrases.english: A certain man
who confined his friend's animal
in the sun, and it died.
Ravina held him liable,
phrases.notes: Liable here means he must pay the owner for the animal.

phrases.english: Rav Aha bar Rav exempted him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the idea of 'confining' from step 21 to a case of damages to an animal.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבינא: one who confines an animal in the sun and it dies must pay. רב אחא בר רב: he is exempt.
steps.confusionAlert: This case is about paying for damage, not the death penalty; it only borrows the idea of confining from שמואל's teaching.

steps.title: רבינא's reasoning: a קל וחומר from a murderer
steps.stepSummary: רבינא proves the confiner must pay with a קל וחומר. The laws of a רוצח are more lenient in some ways, yet the Torah still makes a person who confines someone liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא holds him liable, and he learns it through a קל וחומר: a murderer is a case where the Torah did not treat an accidental killer like a deliberate one, or a forced killer like a willing one. Even so, the Torah made the one who confines a person liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives רבינא's reason for making the man pay for the animal he left in the sun. This line is only the first half of his קל וחומר. The 'all the more so' part comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With murder, the תורה is relatively lenient: someone who kills by accident is not punished like a deliberate killer, and someone who is forced is not punished at all. Even in that lenient area, step 21 showed that confining a person counts as killing. רבינא is building toward the point that damages, which are stricter, should surely make confining count too.

keyTerms.meaning: A logical argument: if a rule holds in the lighter case, it surely holds in the stricter case
A murderer, someone who kills a person
Someone who does it by mistake, without meaning to
Someone who does it on purpose
Someone who is forced, so it is beyond his control
Someone who confines another so he cannot escape

steps.confusionAlert: The קל וחומר is not finished here. This line only shows the lenient side, murder. The stricter side, damages, comes in the next line.

phrases.english: Ravina holds him liable,
phrases.notes: He means liable to pay the owner for the animal that died in the sun (step 22).

phrases.english: learning it through a kal vachomer:
Just as a murderer,
where the Torah did not make unwitting like intentional,
phrases.notes: Someone who kills by accident goes into exile. He is not put to death like a deliberate killer.

phrases.english: and did not make forced like willing,
still made the one who confines liable.
phrases.notes: This is the rule שמואל learned in step 21.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind רבינא's ruling in step 22.
steps.raayaObject: רבינא's ruling that one who confines an animal in the sun must pay for it
steps.raayaSupportSource: A קל וחומר from the laws of murder, where confining a person makes one liable (step 21)
